q-74457.name: Question 1
q-74457.problem:
Suppose that for the angles $u$ and $v,$ we have 

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡u=\frac{3}{5},\,\operatorname{cos}⁡u=\frac{4}{5},\,\operatorname{cos}⁡v=\frac{15}{17}.
$$

Given that $v$ lies in the first quadrant, find the value of $\operatorname{cos}⁡(u-v).$
q-74457.worked_solution:
First, we recall the difference formula for cosine:

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(u-v)=\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v+\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

We know the values of $\operatorname{sin}⁡u$, $\operatorname{cos}⁡u$, and $\operatorname{cos}⁡v.$ To find the missing value of $\operatorname{sin}⁡v,$ we can use the Pythagorean identity:

$$
{sin}^{2}⁡v+{cos}^{2}⁡v=1\,⟹\,{sin}^{2}⁡v=1-{cos}^{2}⁡v
$$

Substituting our values into the Pythagorean identity, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{sin}^{2}⁡v & =1-{cos}^{2}⁡v \\  & =1-{(\frac{15}{17})}^{2} \\  & =1-\frac{{15}^{2}}{{17}^{2}} \\  & =1-\frac{225}{289} \\  & =\frac{289}{289}-\frac{225}{289} \\  & =\frac{64}{289}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡v & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{64}{289}} \\  & =\pm \frac{8}{17}.\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that $v$ lies in the first quadrant, where sine is positive. So, we disregard the negative value, and we have

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡v=\frac{8}{17}.
$$

We can now apply the difference formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(u-v) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v+\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v \\  & =(\frac{4}{5})(\frac{15}{17})+(\frac{3}{5})(\frac{8}{17}) \\  & =\frac{60}{85}+\frac{24}{85} \\  & =\frac{84}{85}\end{aligned}
$$

q-119592.name: Question 2
q-119592.problem:
Suppose that for the angles $u$ and $v,$ we have

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡u=\frac{3}{4},\,\operatorname{cos}⁡u=-\frac{\sqrt{7}}{4},\,\operatorname{cos}⁡v=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.
$$

Given that $v$ lies in the first quadrant, and

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(u-v)=\frac{a\sqrt{2}-b\sqrt{14}}{8},
$$

calculate the value of $a+b.$
q-119592.worked_solution:
First, we recall the difference formula for cosine:

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(u-v)=\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v+\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

We know the values of $\operatorname{sin}⁡u$, $\operatorname{cos}⁡u$, and $\operatorname{cos}⁡v.$ To find the missing value of $\operatorname{sin}⁡v,$ we can use the Pythagorean identity:

$$
{sin}^{2}⁡v+{cos}^{2}⁡v=1\,⟹\,{sin}^{2}⁡v=1-{cos}^{2}⁡v
$$

Substituting our values into the Pythagorean identity, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{sin}^{2}⁡v & =1-{cos}^{2}⁡v \\  & =1-{(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})}^{2} \\  & =1-\frac{(\sqrt{2})^{2}}{{2}^{2}} \\  & =1-\frac{2}{4} \\  & =1-\frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{2}{2}-\frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡v & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{1}{2}} \\  & =\pm \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that $v$ lies in the first quadrant, where sine is positive. So, we disregard the negative value, and we have 

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡v=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.
$$

We can now apply the difference formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(u-v) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v+\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v \\  & =(-\frac{\sqrt{7}}{4})(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})+(\frac{3}{4})(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}) \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{14}}{8}+\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{8} \\  & =\frac{3\sqrt{2}-1\sqrt{14}}{8}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, $a=3,b=1,$ and $a+b=4.$

q-119581.name: Question 4
q-119581.problem:
Suppose that for the angles $u$ and $v,$ we have

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡u=\frac{5}{13},\,\operatorname{sin}⁡v=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},\,\operatorname{cos}⁡v=-\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Given that $u$ lies in the first quadrant, and

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(u+v)=\frac{a\sqrt{3}-b}{26},
$$

calculate the value of $a+b.$
q-119581.worked_solution:
First, we recall the sum formula for cosine:

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(u+v)=\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v-\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

We know the values of $\operatorname{cos}⁡u,$ $\operatorname{sin}⁡v,$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡v.$ To find the missing value of $\operatorname{sin}⁡u,$ we can use the Pythagorean identity:

$$
{sin}^{2}⁡u+{cos}^{2}⁡u=1\,⟹\,{sin}^{2}⁡u=1-{cos}^{2}⁡u
$$

Substituting our values into the Pythagorean identity, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{sin}^{2}⁡u & =1-{cos}^{2}⁡u \\  & =1-{(\frac{5}{13})}^{2} \\  & =1-\frac{{5}^{2}}{{13}^{2}} \\  & =1-\frac{25}{169} \\  & =\frac{169}{169}-\frac{25}{169} \\  & =\frac{144}{169}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡u & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{144}{169}} \\  & =\pm \frac{12}{13}.\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that $u$ lies in the first quadrant, where sine is positive. So, we disregard the negative value, and we have 

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡u=\frac{12}{13}.
$$

We can now apply the sum formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(u+v) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v-\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v \\  & =(\frac{5}{13})(-\frac{1}{2})-(\frac{12}{13})(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}) \\  & =-\frac{5}{26}+\frac{12\sqrt{3}}{26} \\  & =\frac{12\sqrt{3}-5}{26}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, $a=12,b=5,$ and $a+b=17.$

$$

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡u=\frac{5}{7},\,\operatorname{sin}⁡u=-\frac{2\sqrt{6}}{7},\,\operatorname{cos}⁡v=-\frac{1}{2}.
$$

$$

$$

$$

$$

$$

$$

Substituting our values into the Pythagorean identity, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{sin}^{2}⁡v & =1-{cos}^{2}⁡v \\  & =1-{(-\frac{1}{2})}^{2} \\  & =1-\frac{1}{{2}^{2}} \\  & =1-\frac{1}{4} \\  & =\frac{4}{4}-\frac{1}{4} \\  & =\frac{3}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡v & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{3}{4}} \\  & =\pm \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that $v$ lies in the third quadrant, where sine is negative. So, we disregard the positive value, and we have

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡v=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.
$$

We can now apply the sum formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(u+v) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v-\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v \\  & =(\frac{5}{7})(-\frac{1}{2})-(-\frac{2\sqrt{6}}{7})(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}) \\  & =-\frac{5}{14}-\frac{6\sqrt{2}}{14} \\  & =-\frac{6\sqrt{2}+5}{14}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, $a=6,b=5,$ and $a+b=11.$
